Patterns are matched against repository-relative POSIX paths after normalizePath folds backslashes and strips a leading "./". matcherFor expands a pattern to `[p, p/**, **/p, **/p/**]` only when `/[*?[\]{}!]/` does not match it; otherwise the pattern is passed to picomatch verbatim (src/config/exclusions.ts:96-102).

A bare name therefore excludes the directory itself, its descendants, and nested copies — asserted by tests/unit/config-layers.test.ts:243-248 for `node_modules`, `node_modules/pkg/index.js`, `src/node_modules/x.js`.

A trailing-slash pattern has no metacharacter, so it expands to `node_modules/`, `node_modules//**`, `**/node_modules/`, `**/node_modules//**` — all of which require a literal `/` at that position in the input.

src/config/exclusions.ts is unchanged since EPIC-003 apart from a NUL-byte escaping fix (`git log` on that path returns only 9c6a5dc and d1bd70f), so this is current behaviour, not a superseded design.

The [p, p/**, **/p, **/p/**] expansion applies to any metacharacter-free pattern; since commit 70bcfca that test runs after trailing slashes are stripped (src/config/exclusions.ts:103), so the trailing-slash spelling "node_modules/" is expanded exactly like the bare name. Line numbers updated 2026-09-07 (the metacharacter test moved from :98 to :104).␃ferret:content␃

␂ferret:content␂GOTCHA (corrected 2026-09-07, supersedes the "trailing slash excludes nothing" note): an `exclude` pattern with a trailing slash now means exactly what the bare name means. matcherFor strips trailing slashes via withoutTrailingSlash (src/config/exclusions.ts:88-92) before the metacharacter test, so "node_modules/" becomes "node_modules" and gets the [p, p/**, **/p, **/p/**] expansion instead of the four useless forms "node_modules/", "node_modules//**", "**/node_modules/", "**/node_modules//**". Fixed in commit 70bcfca, regression test tests/unit/config-layers.test.ts:250. Two nuances: the slash is stripped from globs too ("docs/**/" behaves as "docs/**"), and the trailing slash does NOT impose gitignore-style directory-only semantics — "secrets/" also excludes a *file* named secrets at any depth, because it is simply the bare-name expansion. A pattern that is only slashes is left as written.␃ferret:content␃

␂ferret:content␂`exclude` accepts a bare glob string or a full rule object {pattern, scope: global|repository|session, reason?, effectiveFrom?} (src/config/exclusions.ts:45-75, src/config/schema.ts:137). Patterns are matched against repository-relative POSIX paths after normalizePath folds backslashes and strips a leading "./". Rules are additive and one-way — effectiveExclusions = DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS (.git, node_modules, .venv, __pycache__, dist, build, coverage, .next, target, vendor) then the user's, and mergeExclusions dedupes on scope+pattern, so a narrower scope can never un-exclude. effectiveFrom gates the rule by evaluation instant. Config layers replace the `exclude` array rather than concatenate it, and FERRET_EXCLUDE is split on commas and semicolons (src/config/resolve.ts:88-94).␃ferret:content␃

␂ferret:content␂Ferret's top-level `exclude` key is enforced in exactly two places today — the repository discovery walk (src/git/discovery.ts:194, via src/git/provider.ts:191) and the read/retrieval path (effectiveExclusions injected into the access context at src/authorization/authorization.ts:287, evaluated per row in src/retrieval/access.ts:249). There is no per-file gate at ingestion: an excluded file inside an indexed repository is still read, stored as entity/version/content_blob, and merely filtered out of answers. EPIC-135 (docs/EPICs/EPIC-135-Exclusion-Enforcement-At-Ingestion.md) specifies the ingestion gate but is status PROPOSED and unimplemented as of 2026-09-07.␃ferret:content␃

answer.conclusion: As the repo stands (HEAD 70bcfca on `phase5-real-agent-ab`), `secrets/` works: `matcherFor` strips the trailing slash and expands the bare name into `secrets`, `secrets/**`, `**/secrets`, `**/secrets/**`, so the directory and everything under it — at any depth — is withheld from every retrieval surface via `withholds`/`visibleEntities`. The answer has not always been the same: until that commit (dated today, and not yet merged to main) the trailing slash produced `secrets//**`-style patterns that matched no path, so the rule was accepted and reported as configured while excluding nothing. One caveat that is still true: exclusion is enforced on the read path only — the files are still read and their content stored (EPIC-135 is PROPOSED, unimplemented), so this keeps `secrets/` out of answers, not out of the database.

answer.conclusion: As the repository stands now, yes: `matcherFor` strips trailing slashes before expanding a metacharacter-free pattern, so `secrets/` compiles to `secrets`, `secrets/**`, `**/secrets`, `**/secrets/**` and withholds the directory and everything under it from answers (`WithholdReason.EXCLUSION` on the read path). This has not always been true — until commit 70bcfca (2026-09-07, on the current branch and not yet on `main`), `secrets/` expanded to `secrets/`, `secrets//**`, `**/secrets/`, `**/secrets//**` and matched no path at all, while still being reported as a configured rule. Two caveats remain: exclusion filters only entities that carry a `path` attribute, and per EPIC-135 (still PROPOSED) the files are still read and stored — only the read path hides them.
key_facts: src/config/exclusions.ts:88-92 defines `withoutTrailingSlash`, and line 103 applies it inside `matcherFor` before the four-form expansion at lines 104-106, so `secrets/` now means what the bare name `secrets` means.
A metacharacter-free pattern expands to `pattern`, `pattern/**`, `**/pattern`, `**/pattern/**` (src/config/exclusions.ts:104-106), which is what makes a bare directory name cover everything under it.

Before the fix, `matcherFor` used `normalizePath(rule.pattern)` with no slash stripping (git show d1bd70f:src/config/exclusions.ts), so `secrets/` produced `secrets//**` and `**/secrets//**` and matched nothing; commit 70bcfca's message states the failure mode was silent — the rule was accepted and reported as configured while excluding nothing.

The fix is commit 70bcfca `fix(config): an exclusion written `secrets/` excluded nothing`, HEAD of branch phase5-real-agent-ab; `git log main..HEAD` shows only that commit, so `main` does not yet contain it.

A regression test was added in the same commit at tests/unit/config-layers.test.ts (`treats a trailing slash as the same directory rule, not as a rule matching nothing`), asserting `node_modules/` excludes `node_modules`, `node_modules/pkg/index.js` and `src/node_modules/x.js`. It could not be executed here: this session is read-only.

The user's `exclude` list is merged with DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS by `effectiveExclusions` (src/config/schema.ts:180-181), and exclusion is additive across scopes (src/config/exclusions.ts:169-181), so adding the entry can only widen what is hidden.

Enforcement on answers runs through `withholds` (src/retrieval/access.ts:246-256) returning `WithholdReason.EXCLUSION`, applied by `visibleEntities` across search, find, neighbours and pack (src/storage/retrieval.ts:394, 453, 703, 1049; src/context/pack.ts:145), and at discovery time in src/git/discovery.ts:194.

`withholds` only evaluates the exclusion when the entity has a non-empty `path` attribute (src/retrieval/access.ts:246-247), so entities without a path — a commit message, for instance — are not filtered by this rule.

docs/EPICs/EPIC-135-Exclusion-Enforcement-At-Ingestion.md is PROPOSED and unimplemented: it records that `exclude` is enforced on the read path only, that excluded files are still read from disk and their full text retained in the store, and that the read surfaces (`ferret_find`, `ferret_search`, `ferret_context_pack`) did return none of them.

A plain string entry becomes a rule with no `effectiveFrom` (src/config/exclusions.ts:72-75), and an omitted `effectiveFrom` means "has always applied" (lines 53-60), so the rule also hides content indexed before it was added.
